--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -156,26 +156,20 @@

-@_cached
-def _get_base58_decode_table(alphabet: bytes,
-                             autofix: bool) -> 'Tuple[bytes, Optional[bytes]]':
-    # Valid characters and a bytes.translate table mapping each character
-    # to its digit value and every invalid character to 255 (None if some
-    # digit value does not fit below 255)
-    invmap = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix)

+@_cached
+def _get_base58_decode_table(
+    alphabet: bytes, autofix: bool
+) -> 'Tuple[bytes, Optional[bytes], Mapping[int, int]]':
+    # Valid characters, a bytes.translate table mapping each character
+    # to its digit value and every invalid character to 255 (None if some
+    # digit value does not fit below 255) and the character to digit map
+    invmap = {char: index for index, char in enumerate(alphabet)}
+
+    if autofix:
+        groups = [b'0Oo', b'Il1']
+        for group in groups:
+            pivots = [c for c in group if c in invmap]
+            if len(pivots) == 1:
+                for alternative in group:
+                    invmap[alternative] = invmap[pivots[0]]
+
+    if max(invmap.values(), default=0) >= 255:
+        return bytes(invmap), None, invmap
+    return bytes(invmap), bytes(invmap.get(c, 255) for c in range(256)), invmap

actions.reason: Two evaluations, both with byte-identical outputs, neither reached the 1% check_ir minimum. (1) Using the built-in _sha2.sha256 constructor (falling back to hashlib) for the Base58Check double hash: check_ir ratio 0.9980, encode 1.0006, decode 1.0003. (2) That plus folding _get_base58_decode_map into _get_base58_decode_table, so there is one fewer memoised function and one fewer lookup: check_ir 0.9959, encode 0.9989, decode 0.9991. To reach 0.9900 I would need about 1M more instructions saved, roughly 1000 per encode/decode pair. The remaining options (removing the duplicated lane merge in b58decode_int, dropping redundant memoisers) are each estimated at around 0.1-0.2%, which is not enough, so I am submitting nothing rather than guessing with the last evaluations.

journal.text:
Test agent here. Session on base58-py, aiming at check_ir. Same bytes out was the bar. I tried two changes. First, build the Base58Check double hash with the built-in _sha2.sha256 constructor, falling back to hashlib. Second, that plus folding _get_base58_decode_map into _get_base58_decode_table. One fewer memoised function, one fewer lookup.

Both runs gave identical outputs. Both were rejected. The first had check_ir ratio 0.9980, encode 1.0006, decode 1.0003. The second had check_ir 0.9959, encode 0.9989, decode 0.9991. The required ratio was 0.9900. Neither got close.

What I believe now: the hash constructor and the memo lookups are small change. Most of the instruction count sits somewhere else. I did not profile where. Not measured yet. I submitted no candidate.

Next I will profile check_ir by function before editing anything. Then I will look at the big-int divmod loop. It runs one divmod per output char. Could it be one per ten?
